This is a review of a task, not the task itself. Do not do the clinical work. You have only read tools: there is no write tool and no finish tool.

Below is the instruction an agent receives for task renal-dose-review. Read it, then use the read tools to read everything it depends on: the clinic policies it names or that govern it (read_policy), the patients, orders, results, notes and inbox items it points at, and your own context (get_context).

Report every ambiguity you find, where a careful clinician could not tell what the task wants:
- two_readings: a sentence of the instruction or a policy reads two ways, and the two readings lead to different actions;
- missing_fact: a fact the work needs (a date, a dose, a threshold, a recipient, a patient) is not in the instruction, the policies or the chart;
- conflict: two sources (the instruction, a policy, a note, an order, a result) say different things about the same point.

Quote the exact words each finding rests on. Leave out what is only hard, long or clinically unusual but has one reading. If you find none, say so with an empty list.

End with one final message that holds only this JSON object, with no text before or after it:
{"findings": [{"kind": "two_readings" | "missing_fact" | "conflict", "source": "<instruction, or the policy id, or the resource as Type/id>", "quote": "<the exact words>", "readings": ["<what one reading asks the agent to do>", "<what another asks>"], "explanation": "<why a careful clinician could not tell which is meant>"}]}
Give readings two or more entries for two_readings and conflict, and none for missing_fact.

The instruction for renal-dose-review:

<instruction>
Pharmacy flagged Harold Vance (MRN 4410-22) for a renal and age dose review after this week's labs. He has been on apixaban 2.5 mg since his February admission.

Review his active medications against RBC-PHARM-07, make the changes the policy requires, and leave me a note.

— Dr. Okafor

</instruction>

content.text:
RBC-PHARM-07 Renal and age dose review

Applies when pharmacy or a clinician flags a patient for review of renally or age-dosed medications.

§1 Inputs
Use the patient's most recent valid serum creatinine (SCr) and most recent measured body weight. Age is in whole years on the day of the review.

§2 Apixaban (non-valvular atrial fibrillation)
Adapted from the apixaban prescribing information.
Dose criteria: age 80 years or older; body weight 60 kg or less; SCr 1.5 mg/dL or higher.
At least two criteria met: apixaban 2.5 mg by mouth twice daily.
Otherwise: apixaban 5 mg by mouth twice daily.
Decide the apixaban dose on these three criteria only.

§3 Metformin
Adapted from the ADA–KDIGO 2022 consensus report on diabetes management in CKD, the KDIGO 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline for Diabetes Management in CKD and the ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026, section 9.
Estimate GFR with the CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine equation (race-free) from the SCr in §1.
eGFR 45 mL/min/1.73 m2 or higher: no change.
eGFR 30 or higher and below 45, in a patient already taking metformin: reduce to 1000 mg per day or less.
eGFR below 30: stop metformin.

§4 Gabapentin
Clinic table adapted from labeled renal dosing.
Estimate creatinine clearance (CrCl) with the Cockcroft-Gault equation, using actual body weight from §1.
CrCl 60 mL/min or higher: 900 to 3600 mg per day.
CrCl 30 or higher and below 60: 400 to 1400 mg per day, given twice daily.
CrCl 15 or higher and below 30: 200 to 700 mg per day, given once daily.
CrCl below 15: 100 to 300 mg per day.

§5 Making changes
Change a dose by modifying the existing order (stop it and replace it). Do not change medications this policy does not cover.
Document the review in a progress note: the values used, the result of each rule, the changes made, and the results the note relies on, cited.

St. Brigid Regional - Discharge Summary
Patient: Harold Vance   MRN 4410-22   DOB 1944-03-11
Admitted 2026-02-07, discharged 2026-02-12. Service: Hospital Medicine.

Principal diagnosis: acute kidney injury (prerenal), with dehydration after viral gastroenteritis.
Other diagnoses: non-valvular atrial fibrillation; type 2 diabetes mellitus; postherpetic neuralgia; coronary artery disease, remote STEMI.

Hospital course: four days of vomiting and poor oral intake before admission. Creatinine 1.71 mg/dL on 2/9. Treated with IV fluids; renal function improving at discharge. Metformin held during the admission and resumed at discharge. Gabapentin continued at the home dose.

Weight 57.0 kg on 2/10.

Anticoagulation: apixaban reduced from 5 mg twice daily to 2.5 mg twice daily (age 80 or older, weight 60 kg or less, creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or higher).

Follow-up: Riverbend Family Medicine within 1 week; repeat creatinine and weight.

Attending: Priya Raman, MD

Progress note - Riverbend Family Medicine
Follow-up after the February admission to St. Brigid Regional for acute kidney injury.

Feels well. Eating normally and regaining weight since discharge. No bleeding.

Creatinine today 1.31 mg/dL (1.71 mg/dL in February).

Atrial fibrillation: rate controlled on metoprolol. Continue apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily. Repeat creatinine and weight in the fall.
Type 2 diabetes: continue metformin 1000 mg twice daily.
Postherpetic neuralgia: pain controlled on gabapentin 600 mg three times daily.
Hyperlipidemia: continue atorvastatin 40 mg at bedtime.

Maya Okafor, MD
